Fusion · The Seoul Table

Gochujang-Miso Black Cod

Two fermented pastes meet delicate black cod in this Korean-Japanese fusion dish.

Korean-Japanese-American · Easy · Serves 4

Jump to recipe ↓

Behind the dish

Lane: fusion — two ferments and a fish. The famous miso-marinated black cod, rebuilt with the paste in the cure: white miso for its sweetness, gochujang for its heat and depth, a short 24-hour cure where the grill-site's version (#SF11's doenjang build) runs 48 with a different register. This is the weeknight version of the luxury fish — the cure takes ten minutes today and dinner takes twelve tomorrow. Heat dial: 2.

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Whisk the cure to one color — miso and gochujang are both stiff pastes; work them with the mirin and honey until uniform rust, then the sesame oil. Paint every fillet face thick, stack in a dish, cover, refrigerate 24 hours (12 at the floor; past 36 the salt tightens the flesh).
  • Scrape the excess cure to a thin film before cooking — leave the coat, lose the clumps (a thick clump burns before the fish glazes).

Let’s make it.

  1. 01
    A heavy pan at medium with the film of oil; fillets in presentation-side-down, 4 minutes to deep tea-brown caramel — the sugars' clock, watched, not set-and-forgotten. Checkpoint — the face lifts clean and reads dark caramel, not black. Smoking hard: the heat is a notch past the sugars' tolerance — lower and give the pan a minute.
  2. 02
    Flip, 3 minutes more on the second side (a fillet's thickness giving 7 minutes total on the pan), and pull at the flake stage — the flesh parts along the grain at a fork's weight, translucent-glossy at the very center. Checkpoint — the test flake: lacquered outside, butter-silk inside, the two ferments' depth all the way through — miso's sweetness and the paste's warm hum arriving one after the other. That sequence is the fusion's signature.
  3. 03
    Sesame and scallion over, plated on rice with the sharp pickle beside. Checkpoint — the eating test with the pickle in the same bite-set: rich, savory-sweet, a late warmth, then the acid's reset. If the heat reads before the miso, the gochujang ran heavy — a tablespoon less next cure. Chef’s Note — why this cure runs shorter than the grill-site's 48-hour doenjang build: white miso and gochujang are both faster, sweeter, saltier workers than doenjang — they penetrate quickly and then start curing hard, where the deeper doenjang gives and keeps giving. Two ferments at 24 hours hit the same depth-with-tenderness the single deep one reaches at 48. Same fish, different clocks, honestly different dishes — try both across two weekends and the pastes' speeds will teach you more than any essay.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cure burnt on the panThick clumps left onScrape to a thin film before cooking
Fish salt-tightCured past 36 hours24 is the target; 12 the floor
Heat swamped the misoGochujang-heavy jarA tablespoon less; taste the jar first
Fell apart at the flipThin spatula, soft fishFull support, one confident turn

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Curing fillets hold 36 hours (the clock above); cooked, 2 days — cold flakes over rice with sesame oil is the day-after luxury.
  • Variations: salmon at a 12-hour cure; the braise-glaze (#1) thinned as a warm sauce over; a drop of honey in the final minute under the broiler for the lacquered ceiling.
